subject: MAP & commercial playbook: evaluation milestones, commits, and region premiums
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Josef Lee <j.lee@acme.com>; Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & commercial playbook: evaluation milestones, commits, and region premiums

Josef / Acme team,

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concise mutual action plan (MAP) on your calendar that ties the evaluation milestones to the commercial terms so procurement can see clear triggers for pricing, committed throughput, and any multi-region residency premiums. Attaching a draft MAP (MAP_Acme_v1.xlsx) and a short SOW outline.

High level proposal (please see the attachment for week-by-week detail):
- Week 1–2 (Eval): Integration + baseline perf tests — no commit, free eval credits.
- Week 3–4 (Pilot): Production-like workload — if pilot achieves 95% of target latency/throughput, Acme signs a 6-month committed capacity at Tier 1 pricing.
- Month 3+: Ramp — committed increase to Tier 2 at a negotiated uplift if Acme reaches 2x baseline tokens/day within the quarter.

Commercial tie-ins we propose:
- Pricing: baseline per-token rate for US region; a residency surcharge (one-time setup + ongoing premium) for EU data residency.
- Commits: discount schedule tied to committed GPU-hours/month (see MAP tab).
- Failover: cross-region failover will carry a separate SLA surcharge and a per-token egress adjustment when traffic crosses regions.

Open items we need from Acme to finalize: primary residency region(s), expected peak tokens/day, and any specific compliance evidence required for your EU workloads.

Next steps: can we align on these MAP milestones and the associated commercial triggers by next Wednesday (4/15)? If yes, we can issue a redline SOW and a DocuSign-ready order form.

Thanks,

Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: MAP_Acme_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: SOW_draft_Acme.pdf (PDF)

From: Josef Lee <j.lee@acme.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & commercial playbook: evaluation milestones, commits, and region premiums

Grace,

Thanks for the clear plan — this is exactly the structure procurement likes to see. A couple of clarifying points from our side: 

1) Residency: our initial pilot must keep EU customer PII in EU. We'll be US-first for non-PII, but need the EU residency option scoped and priced.
2) Failover: we'll need guaranteed regional failover latency targets and an estimate of additional cost when failover traffic runs out of EU region to the US. Can you put both a setup fee and an ongoing per-request surcharge in the MAP?
3) Timing: 4/15 is tight for procurement review; can we target 4/20 instead?

Otherwise the MAP looks good. Procurement will add a short list of required clauses (data residency, audit rights, indemnity caps) and we'll send that back.

—Josef
Josef Lee
Head of ML Infrastructure | Acme Corp
j.lee@acme.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-13T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP & commercial playbook: evaluation milestones, commits, and region premiums

Folks — forwarding Josef's reply. Procurement wants the EU residency scoped + failover uplift broken into (a) one-time setup, (b) monthly residency premium, and (c) per-token/egress adjustment during failover. Also asked for latency targets for cross-region failover.

Can you two draft a short commercial Appendix that:
- Defines the residency premium (percent uplift on list price, or fixed USD per committed GPU-hour)
- States the failover surcharge model (flat per-token vs. capped monthly charge)
- Includes example math for a 1M token/day and 5M token/day profile so Acme can see unit economics

Karthik — can you also confirm whether we can offer an initial one-month "grace" where failover egress is waived for test runs? That helps them get comfortable with the pilot.

Dylan — can you build two example pricing tables (US-only; US+EU with residency premium + failover uplift) and attach to the appendix. We should keep the MAP milestones unchanged but add the Appendix as the commercial attachment.

Goal: have Appendix + redline SOW back to Acme by 4/20.

Thanks,
Grace

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-16T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP & commercial playbook: evaluation milestones, commits, and region premiums

Grace / Dylan — attaching a first draft Appendix in the thread (see SOW page 2) and two quick pricing scenarios. Highlights: 

- Residency premium: we suggest a setup fee of $12,500 (one-time) + a 15% ongoing uplift on list tokens price for EU-resident workloads. Alternatively we can offer a fixed $/GPU-hour uplift of $0.45/hr for committed pools in EU.
- Failover surcharge: waive egress for the first 30 days for pilot (one-month grace) as discussed. After that, failover traffic billed at +10% per-token premium when traffic leaves the resident region, with a monthly cap equal to 5% of committed spend (protects against runaway charges).
- Latency targets: cross-region failover SLO of p95 < 220ms for short prompts, p95 < 420ms for long-context responses (documented in Appendix B). These are conservative; we can tighten with dedicated routing (premium).

Example math included: 1M tokens/day => incremental monthly residency uplift ~$4,750 under percent model vs ~$3,900 under GPU-hour uplift model (numbers in spreadsheet).

If Acme prefers, we can propose a hybrid: percent uplift for token-heavy calls + per-GPU-hour uplift for dedicated throughput guarantees.

I can export the Appendix to PDF and redline SOW if we have internal approval on these numbers.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
